editorial:
Imagine a guy who had it all as a star football player but walked away from the game. Now, Pierre spends his nights doing magic tricks at a cabaret and spending his days spying for the police. He is stuck in a weird spot, living with his girlfriend Marie, a singer who wants to make it big in show business. While Pierre is just trying to keep his head down and ignore the bad memories from his time in the Algerian War, things start to get messy. The vibe is kind of moody and tense, making you feel like something bad is about to happen even when things seem quiet.

You will really feel for Pierre as a mean inspector starts playing games with him just to get a promotion. The way the plot twists and turns is great, and the acting feels very real. It is not a fast movie, but it builds up a lot of pressure. If you like stories about people caught in traps they cannot escape, you should definitely check this out. You can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, or if you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends with Pierre realizing he is just a pawn in the inspector's game. The villain tries to frame him and his boss, but the plan backfires. After a lot of tension and pressure, the truth about the manipulation comes out. Pierre manages to survive the trap, but he is left emotionally drained. He finds out that the people he trusted were just using him, leaving him to wonder if he can ever truly start over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school crime dramas and character studies.
